comments.author: Alex Kim
comments.body: CSS fix in heatmap.module.css ships with forced-colors media queries; a11y review signed off.

content.text: CSS fix in heatmap.module.css ships with forced-colors media queries; a11y review signed off.

Dashboard activity heatmaps look correct in normal themes. Under Windows forced colors / high-contrast mode (or forced-colors: active), every cell paints fully transparent so the grid is an empty frame with axis labels only.

Cells must remain distinguishable in forced colors, typically via system color pairs (Canvas / Highlight) or explicit forced-color-adjust handling. Currently fill comes from CSS variables that resolve to transparent when the browser overrides the palette.

Heatmap cells set background-color to var(--heat-n) without a forced-colors fallback, and forced-color-adjust: none was never set. Adding system-color borders and a non-transparent fallback fill restored the grid for high-contrast users.
